folios.unwan_text: مَبْحَثُ اتِّحَادِ الفَاعِلِ وَالمَفْعُولِ فِي الضَّمِيرِ المُنْفَصِلِ وَأَحْكَامِ التَّوْكِيدِ
diplomatic_matn: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
الجَوَابُ بِحَمْدِ اللهِ وَحُسْنِ عَوْنِهِ وَصَلَّى اللهُ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِهِ:
قَالَ الشَّيْخُ الإِمَامُ أَبُو سَعِيدٍ فَرَجُ بْنُ قَاسِمِ بْنِ لُبٍّ الغَرْنَاطِيُّ رحه:
اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الفَاعِلَ وَالمَفْعُولَ إِذَا اتَّحَدَا فِي الضَّمِيرِ المُنْفَصِلِ امْتَنَعَ تَقْدِيمُهُ
وَأَمَّا التَّوْكِيدُ اللَّفْظِيُّ وَالمَعْنَوِيُّ فَيَجْرِي عَلَى مَذْهَبِ سِيبَوَيْهِ وَالبَصْرِيِّينَ
وَهَذَا تَحْقِيقُ المَسَائِلِ النَّحْوِيَّةِ الَّتِي أَلْغَزَ فِيهَا النَّاظِمُ اهـ

وَهَذَا تَحْقِيقُ المَسَائِلِ النَّحْوِيَّةِ الَّتِي أَلْغَزَ فِيهَا النَّاظِمُ [انْتَهَى]
english_lines: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
The Answer, with praise to Allah and His gracious aid, and blessings upon our Master Muḥammad and his family:
The Shaykh and Imām Abū Saʿīd Faraj ibn Qāsim Ibn Lubb al-Gharnāṭī (may Allah have mercy on him) said:
Know that when the grammatical agent (al-Fāʿil) and object (al-Mafʿūl) coincide in a detached pronoun, fronting it is prohibited.
As for verbal and semantic emphasis (al-Tawkīd), it proceeds according to the school of Sībawayh and the Baṣran grammarians.
And this is the critical verification of the syntactic problems versified as riddles by the poet. [End of Preliminary Section]

folios.unwan_text: القَصِيدَةُ اللُّغْزِيَّةُ فِي المَسَائِلِ النَّحْوِيَّةِ لِلإِمَامِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ فَرَجِ بْنِ قَاسِمِ بْنِ لُبٍّ التَّغْلِبِيِّ

الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي أَسْمَاءَ الأَفْعَالِ مِثْلَ (صَهٍ) وَ(مَهٍ) وَ(إِيهٍ) فَمَا نُوِّنَ مِنْهَا فَهُوَ نَكِرَةٌ وَمَا لَمْ يُنَوَّنْ فَمَعْرِفَةٌ اهـ

english_lines: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
I praise my Lord with the praise of one in humble submission, confessing with both heart and tongue,
invoking blessings upon the Chosen Messenger, in whom both secret and open devotion are enraptured.
Thereafter: since you asked me regarding intricate grammatical problems (Masāʾil fī al-Naḥw) of subtle difficulty,
I have composed for you verses wherein the correct ruling shines forth like a demonstrative proof (ka-al-Burhān).
Riddle #1: 'What indeclinable noun is predicate to a definite referent while bearing Tanwīn to mark indefiniteness?'
Commentary: He means verbal nouns (Asmāʾ al-Afʿāl) such as 'Ṣahin' (Hush!) and 'Mahin' (Stop!): when nunated they are indefinite, and when un-nunated they are definite. [End]

folios.folio_label: Folio 3b — Riddles #2 (Bāb al-Nidāʾ), #3 (Asmāʾ al-Shurūṭ) & #4 (Ḍamīr al-Shaʾn)
folios.unwan_text: حَلُّ الأَلْغَازِ فِي بَابِ النِّدَاءِ وَأَسْمَاءِ الشُّرُوطِ وَضَمِيرِ الشَّأْنِ وَالقِصَّةِ

الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي بَابَ النِّدَاءِ مِثْلَ (يَا زَيْدُ الظَّرِيفُ وَالظَّرِيفَ) فَتَابِعُ المُنَادَى يُرَاعَى فِيهِ اللَّفْظُ بِالرَّفْعِ وَالمَوْضِعُ بِالنَّصْبِ

الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي أَسْمَاءَ الشُّرُوطِ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿أَيًّا مَّا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الأَسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾ فَيَعْمَلُ فِيهَا الابْتِدَاءُ وَالشَّرْطِيَّةُ
اللُّغْزُ الرَّابِعُ: وَمَا مُفْرَدُ اللَّفْظِ لَهُ مَعْنَى كَلَامٍ * مُذَكَّرٌ إِنْ شِئْتَ أَوْ مُؤَنَّثٌ فِي الرَّفْعِ وَالنَّصْبِ:
الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي ضَمِيرَ الشَّأْنِ وَالقِصَّةِ المَفَسَّرَ بِالجُمْلَةِ بَعْدَهُ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ اهـ

english_lines: Riddle #2: 'What class of indeclinable noun possesses two syntactic statuses in utterance, such that its follower may concord with either?'
Commentary: He means the Vocative (Bāb al-Nidāʾ), e.g., 'Yā Zaydu al-Ẓarīfu / al-Ẓarīfa': the appositive may take nominative by formal vowel or accusative by underlying syntactic place.
Riddle #3: 'What element governs in its syntactic locus while two abstract semantic operators govern it?'

Commentary: He means Conditional Nouns (Asmāʾ al-Shurūṭ), as in Q. 17:110 ('Whichever you call upon, to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names'), governed jointly by inchoation (Ibtidāʾ) and conditionality.
Riddle #4: 'What formally singular word carries the meaning of an entire proposition, masculine or feminine, in nominative or accusative?'
Commentary: He means the Pronoun of the Matter/Story (Ḍamīr al-Shaʾn wa-al-Qiṣṣah) explained by the clause following it, as in Q. 112:1 ('Say: He is Allah, the One'). [End]

folios.unwan_text: أَلْغَازُ القَلْبِ المَكَانِيِّ فِي (أَيْنُق) وَ(جَاه) وَجَمْعِ المُذَكَّرِ السَّالِمِ وَنَقلِ الحَرَكَةِ
diplomatic_matn: اللُّغْزُ الخَامِسُ: وَمَا فِعْلٌ تَحَوَّلَ فِيهِ حَرْفٌ * إِلَى مَوْضِعِ الفَاءِ قَبْلَ العَيْنِ:
الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي مَسْأَلَةَ (أَيْنُقٍ) جَمْعِ نَاقَةٍ فَأَصْلُهُ أَنْوُقٌ فَقُدِّمَتِ العَيْنُ إِلَى مَوْضِعِ الفَاءِ وَقُلِبَتْ يَاءً بِالقَلْبِ المَكَانِيِّ

اللُّغْزُ السَّادِسُ: وَمَا كَلِمَةٌ تَعْرَى فَلَا وُجُودَ لِحَرْفِهَا * بِوَاوٍ وَفِي يَا ذَلِكَ الحَرْفُ يُوجَدُ:
الشَّرْحُ: يَعْنِي نَحْوَ (مُصْطَفَوْنَ) وَ(الأَعْلَوْنَ) وَ(القَاضُونَ) حُذِفَتْ لَامُ الكَلِمَةِ عِنْدَ الوَاوِ وَاليَاءِ لِالْتِقَاءِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ

Commentary: He means the plural 'Aynuq' (she-camels, from Nāqah): its underlying form is 'Anwuq', where the medial radical shifted and turned to Yāʾ by metathesis (al-Qalb al-Makānī).
Abū al-Qāsim al-Zajjājī stated regarding 'Jāh' (prestige, from Wajh): the medial radical was fronted before the initial radical, yielding the morphological pattern 'ʿAfal'.
Riddle #6: 'What word loses its final radical when inflected with Wāw or Yāʾ in the plural?'
Commentary: He means defective/shortened plurals like 'Muṣṭafawna', 'al-Aʿlawna', and 'al-Qāḍūna', where the final radical drops before the plural Wāw/Yāʾ to prevent two quiescents.
Riddle #7: 'What definite noun functions as object or subject [i.e., Ayyuhum]?' followed by the phonological riddle of 'al-Biʾr' under vowel transfer (Naql al-Ḥarakah). [End]
hashiyah_lines: حاشية أندلسية: قال أبو القاسم الزجاجي في جاه: أصله وجه فقدم العين على الفاء، صح.

اللُّغْزُ الرَّابِعَ عَشَرَ: وَمَا اسْمٌ يَكُونُ فِعْلاً وَحَرْفاً * فَيَنْصِبُ تَارَةً وَيَجُرُّ أُخْرَى:

english_lines: Riddle #13: 'What morphological cause bars a word from triptote declension (Ṣarf), yet when the feminine Tāʾ enters it, diptote restriction ceases?'
Commentary: He means broken plurals of the extreme pattern like 'Ṣayārif' vs. 'Ṣayārifah' and 'Malāʾik' vs. 'Malāʾikah': adding Hāʾ al-Jamʿ restores full triptote declension.
Riddle #14: 'What word functions both as a verb and a particle, governing the accusative at times and the genitive at others?'
Commentary: He means the exceptive particles 'Ḥāshā', 'Khalā', and 'ʿAdā' in Istithnāʾ, which govern the accusative as verbs and the genitive as prepositions.
Riddle #15: 'What word is followed by nouns in the nominative at times and in the genitive at others?'
Commentary: He means temporal 'Mudh' and 'Mundhu', after which nouns take the nominative or genitive depending on whether they are construed as predicates or prepositions. [End]

english_lines: Riddle #23: 'What grammatically definite noun refers to no specific external individual yet is barred from triptote declension?'
Commentary: He means 'Ladun Ghadwata' (at early morning), where 'Ghadwata' is diptote due to generic proper-noun status (ʿAlamiyyah Jinsiyyah) and femininity, as stated by Sībawayh.
Riddle #24: 'What syntactic governor has its governed element absorbed inside it without being a pronoun?'
Commentary: He means 'Ithnā ʿAshara' (twelve), where 'ʿAshara' stands in place of the dual Nūn of 'Ithnāni', so one cannot say 'Ithnā ʿAshara ʿAshara'.
Riddle #25: 'What particle is added to reinforce meaning between preposition and genitive, as in Q. 3:159 (Fa-bimā Raḥmatin min Allāhi)?'
Commentary: He means the augmentative 'Mā' inserted between preposition and genitive for rhetorical emphasis without canceling genitive government. [End]

english_lines: Riddle #39: 'What word appears in the surface pattern of Afʿāl yet is a collective noun barred from triptote nunation?'
Commentary: He means 'Ashyāʾ' (plural of Shayʾ), as in Q. 5:101 ('O you who believe, do not ask about things [Ashyāʾa] which, if shown to you, would distress you').

Its morphological measure according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl is 'Lafʿāʾu' (from Shayʾāʾu via initial metathesis of the Hamzah); according to al-Akhfash 'Afʿilāʾu'; and according to al-Farrāʾ 'Afʿālu'.
Riddle #40: 'What two verbs contend over a single syntactic argument such that one governs it overtly and the other via pronominalization?'
Commentary: He means Syntactic Contention (Bāb al-Tanāzuʿ), e.g., 'Ḍarabanī wa-Ḍarabtu Zaydan' and Imruʾ al-Qays's verse 'Kafānī wa-lam Aṭlub Qalīlun min al-Māli'.
Riddle #41: 'What definite article functions as a relative pronoun (al-Mawṣūlah) entering upon explicit participles?' [End]

Commentary: He means Quoting Indefinites (Ḥikāyat al-Nakirāt) via 'Man', saying 'Manū' in the nominative, 'Manā' in the accusative, and 'Manī' in the genitive.
Concluding Verse (V. 70): 'And with these SEVENTY [verses] is completed a Qaṣīdah upon the sciences of the Arabic tongue (ʿalā Funūn al-Lisān)!'
'Its sections finely articulated, you shall behold it adorned with rubies and pearls (Yawāqīt al-Jumān).'

diplomatic_matn: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ
قَالَ أَبُو اللَّيْثِ السَّمَرْقَنْدِيُّ وَالنَّسَفِيُّ رَحِمَهُمَا اللهُ فِي تَفْسِيرِ (بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ):
إِنَّ البَاءَ لِلإِلْصَاقِ وَالِاسْتِعَانَةِ أَوِ المُصَاحَبَةِ وَهُمَا مَجَازَانِ فِي الطَّرَفَيْنِ، وَالمُتَعَلَّقُ مَحْذُوفٌ تَقْدِيرُهُ (أَبْتَدِئُ) أَوِ (ابْتِدَائِي)
وَأَوْرَدَ الشَّعْرَانِيُّ فِي مَبْحَثِ البَسْمَلَةِ أَنَّ تَقْدِيمَ الجَارِّ وَالمَجْرُورِ يُفِيدُ الِاخْتِصَاصَ وَالحَصْرَ
فَإِنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ حُذِفَتِ الأَلِفُ مِنْ (بِسْمِ اللهِ) فِي الخَطِّ العُثْمَانِيِّ؟ قِيلَ: لِكَثْرَةِ الِاسْتِعْمَالِ وَأُبْقِيَتْ فِي نَحْوِ ﴿ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾
وَالبَسْمَلَةُ مُشْتَمِلَةٌ عَلَى أَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ وَتِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفاً فِي رَسْمِ المُصْحَفِ الإِمَامِ اهـ

english_lines: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
Abū al-Layth al-Samarqandī and al-Nasafī (may Allah have mercy on them) stated regarding the exegesis of 'Bismi Allāhi al-Raḥmāni al-Raḥīm':
The preposition Bāʾ denotes adhesion/assistance (Istiʿānah) or accompaniment (Muṣāḥabah), linked to an elided verb ('I begin') or verbal noun ('My beginning').
Al-Shaʿrānī noted in his discourse on the Basmalah that fronting the prepositional phrase imparts exclusivity and restriction (al-Ikhtiṣāṣ wa-al-Ḥaṣr).
If it is asked: Why was the Alif elided from 'Bismi Allāhi' in Uthmānī orthography? Because of high frequency of usage, whereas it is retained in Q. 96:1 ('Iqraʾ bi-ismi Rabbika').
And the Basmalah comprises four words and nineteen letters in the orthography of the Master Uthmānī Codex. [End of Tetouan MS 38]

english_lines: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
Varieties of cooling dishes (al-Bawārid) are prepared from gourd (al-Qarʿ), yogurt (al-Māst), and purslane with verjuice and pomegranate juice;
when the patient's temperament is constipated/dry, plum water and tamarind are used together with beet roots, gourd, hulled almond, and sugar.
When accompanied by insomnia (Qillah fī al-Nawm), administer Nabūsaq compounded from gourd, beet roots, orache (al-Qaṭaf), and cucumber.
For Hot Cephalalgia with humoral matter (al-Ṣudāʿ al-Ḥārr maʿa Māddah), gently purge the bowels with 10–20 fresh or soaked plums followed by rosewater Jullāb.
Cold water benefits headache accompanied by facial flushing and vascular engorgement, while sour pomegranate juice should be avoided. [Catchword: al-Rummān]

english_lines: [...pomegranate] and lentils and similar foods that thicken the blood; whoever suffers headache after sleep should hasten to take nourishment.
For Cold Cephalalgia (al-Ṣudāʿ al-Bārid), white meat broths (Isfīdhbājāt), braised dishes (Muṭajjanāt), spiced pan-roasts (Qalāyā), and attenuating foods are indicated.
Chickpea broth dressed with olive oil and cumin, as well as lean meat sautéed with pepper and cinnamon (Dārṣīnī), is beneficial for them.
Honey is more suitable than sugar provided no concurrent symptom contraindicates it.
For headache arising fromviscous phlegmatic humor, squill oxymel (al-Sakanjabīn al-ʿUnṣulī) and warm water relieve cold or flatulent cephalalgia.
The patient with vaporous headache is fed washed bread, soft-boiled eggs (Nīmbirisht), and lettuce (al-Khass), which extinguishes ascending vapors. [End]

folios.unwan_text: بَابٌ فِي تَدْبِيرِ أَغْذِيَةِ النَّاقِهِينَ مِنَ البِرْسَامِ وَمُدَاوَاةِ أَوْجَاعِ العَيْنِ

Convalescents recovering from phrenitis/pleurisy (al-Birsām) must especially avoid hot foods and indigestion (al-Tukhamah) more than any other patients.

english_lines: [...and] vinegar-braised meats (Maṣūṣ), broths, and calf-jelly (Hulām al-ʿAjājīl); for visual weakness from excess moisture and incipient cataract, pan-roasts and roasts are indicated,
and dishes containing asafoetida (al-Ḥiltīt), fermented condiment (al-Murrī), and honey suit them, along with all desiccating regimens.
For Epistaxis (li-al-Ruʿāf): strongly chilled foods cooled upon snow/ice—such as sour yogurt stew, pomegranate stew, apple stew, sumac stew, and lentil stew;
fresh moist cheese suits epistaxis patients, and chicken brains (Admighat al-Dajāj) are among the finest foods and remedies for nosebleed caused by trauma or a fall.
For Hot Oral Affections—aphthae (al-Qulāʿ), hot oral pustules, and quinsy (al-Khawānīq): sour-astringent fruits such as quince, verjuice, barberry, and Damascus mulberry;
this benefits early hot angina, hot gingival inflammation, and tonsillar swelling, while cold toothache is relieved by chewing coconut (Nārjīl), walnut, and figs with nutmeg. [Catchword: Qalīl]

english_lines: The first principle of Medicine is knowing the temperament of remedies and diagnosing which of the four humors (al-Akhlāṭ al-Arbaʿah) causes the disease:
Verse: 'If yellow bile—hot and dry in nature—prevails, treat it by contraries (bi-al-Aḍdād) once prepared for purgation!'
Yellow Bile (al-Ṣafrāʾ) is generated from the natural element of Fire, and its anatomical seat in the human body is the Gallbladder (al-Marārah);
Phlegm (al-Balgham) is cold and moist, generated from the natural element of Water, and its anatomical seat in man is the Lung (al-Riʾah);
Black Bile (al-Sawdāʾ) is cold and dry, generated from the element of Earth, and its anatomical seat in man is the Spleen (al-Ṭiḥāl);
Blood (al-Dam) is hot and moist, generated from the element of Air, and its anatomical seat in man is the Liver (al-Kabid). [End]

english_lines: The Book of Medicine, with Allah's aid: First I begin with Alopecia Areata (Dāʾ al-Thaʿlab), wherein the hair sheds; the scalp is shaved and rubbed vigorously with bran and salt.
This condition is named 'Fox Disease' (Dāʾ al-Thaʿlab) because it frequently afflicts foxes; its etiology is putrid melancholic or phlegmatic humor corrupting the hair follicles.
If caused by heat (indicated by scalp erythema), treatment is cephalic vein phlebotomy (Faṣd al-Qīfāl), systemic purgation, and fruit decoctions of plum and tamarind fortified with scammony.
If caused by cold (indicated by pallor of the patch), treatment is purging the cold humor, gargling with phlegm-drawing mustard and honey, and anointing with rue, gum, nigella, and olive oil.
A related condition is Ophiasis (Dāʾ al-Ḥayyah, 'Serpent Disease'), so named because the skin peels like a serpent's slough; its treatment follows that of Alopecia Areata.

Chapter on Restoring and Treating Hair (Iṣlāḥ al-Shaʿr): when dry and brittle, anoint with psyllium mucilage (Bazr Qaṭūnā), violet oil, sesame oil (Shīraj), and liquid storax (al-Mayʿah al-Sāʾilah). [End]

إِذَا عَايَنْتَ سَيْلَ الحُبِّ غَمْرَا * وَقَدْ مُلِئَتْ بِكَ الأَعْدَاءُ غِمْرَا * فَلَا تَكُ فِي الهَوَى يَا صَاحِ غُمْرَا
بِفَتْحِ الغَيْنِ قُلْ مَاءٌ كَثِيرٌ * وَحِقْدٌ إِنْ كَسَرْتَ بِهِ جَدِيرٌ * وَقُلْ بِالضَّمِّ غِرٌّ مُسْتَحِيرٌ
وَبِفَتْحِ السِّينِ (سَلَامٌ) لِمَنْ تُنَادِي * وَبِالكَسْرِ الحِجَارَةُ يَا سِنَادِي * وَبِالضَّمِّ الرَّوَاهِشُ فِي الأَيَادِي

english_lines: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
Says the humble servant Sālim ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd ibn Salmān al-Dubaysī al-Mazīdī (may Allah have mercy on him):
Verse: 'When you behold the torrent of love abundant (Ghamrā), while foes are filled with malice (Ghimrā), be not naive (Ghumrā)!'
Gloss: With Fatḥah (Ghamr) it means abundant water; with Kasrah (Ghimr), hidden rancor; with Ḍammah (Ghumr), an inexperienced novice.
With Fatḥah (Salām) it is a greeting; with Kasrah (Silām), solid stones; with Ḍammah (Sulām), the dorsal bones/tendons of the hand.
With Fatḥah (Ẓalm) it is the luster of teeth; with Kasrah (Ẓilm), snow/water; with Ḍammah (Ẓulm), wrongdoing and injustice. [End]
hashiyah_lines: حاشية: جعلت أول كلامي مكتوباً بالحمرة ليمتاز من كلام الشيخ الديريني رحمه الله.

folios.folio_label: Folio 3a — Tri-Vocalic Roots: Ḥalm, Lahā, Samām, Daʿwah, Sharb, Kharq
folios.unwan_text: فَصْلٌ فِي مُثَلَّثَاتِ (حَلْم) وَ(لَهَا) وَ(سَمَام) وَ(دَعْوَة) وَ(شَرْب) وَ(خَرْق)

english_lines: Verse: 'The estrangement of loved ones wasted the body (Ḥalmā), leaving the lover no forbearance (Ḥilmā); had he tasted sleep or seen a dream-vision (Ḥulmā)!'
Gloss: With Fatḥah (Ḥalm) it means hide-tick/skin decay; with Kasrah (Ḥilm), gravity and clemency; with Ḍammah (Ḥulm), a dream in sleep.
With Fatḥah (Lahā) it means the uvula/upper throat; with Kasrah (Lihā), the grain handful cast into the millstone; with Ḍammah (Luhā), munificent gifts.
Verse: 'The caller of consolation called (Daʿwah), yet his false claim (Diʿwah) is naught beside the banquet (Duʿwah)!'
Gloss: With Fatḥah (Daʿwah) it is supplication/invitation; with Kasrah (Diʿwah), a false lineage claim; with Ḍammah (Duʿwah), a hospitality feast.
With Fatḥah (Kharq) it is a vast desert; with Kasrah (Khirq), a generous noble youth; with Ḍammah (Khurq), folly and awkwardness. [End]
hashiyah_lines: حاشية: وبفتح الشين (شَرْب) اسم للندامى، وبالكسر النصيب في الماء، وبالضم المصدر، صح.

folios.folio_label: Folio 4a — Tri-Vocalic Roots: Laḥā, Malā, Shakl, Ṣarrah, Rammah, ʿAmr
folios.unwan_text: فَصْلٌ فِي مُثَلَّثَاتِ (لَحَا) وَ(مَلَا) وَ(شَكْل) وَ(صَرَّة) وَ(رَمَّة) وَ(عَمْر)
diplomatic_matn: زَهَا فَدَعِ اللِّحَا وَاتْرُكْ مَلَامِي * فَبِفَتْحِ اللَّامِ اسْمٌ لِلخِصَامِ * وَإِنْ تَكْسِرْ فَجَمْعٌ لِلِّحْيَةِ وَالضَّمُّ شَعْرُ الذَّقَنِ
وَبِفَتْحِ المِيمِ (مَلَا) خَبْتٌ ذُو فَضَاءِ * وَإِنْ تَكْسِرْ فَمِلْءٌ لِلإِنَاءِ * وَبِالضَّمِّ الثِّيَابُ فَخُذْ حِبَائِي
وَبِفَتْحِ الشِّينِ (شَكْلٌ) مِثْلٌ فِي التَّحَاذِي * وَإِنْ تَكْسِرْ فَدَلُّ الالْتِذَاذِ * وَإِنْ تَضْمُمْ فَقَيْدٌ لَسْتُ هَاذِي
وَبِفَتْحِ الصَّادِ (صَرَّةٌ) اسْمٌ لِلجَمَاعَهْ * وَبَرْدٌ إِنْ كَسَرْتَ لِذَاكَ سَاعَهْ * وَإِنْ تَضْمُمْ مِنَ المَالِ اجْتِمَاعَهْ
وَبِفَتْحِ الرَّاءِ (رَمَّةٌ) إِصْلَاحُ الفَسَادِ * وَبِالكَسْرِ الهَلَاكُ وَالعِظَامُ البَالِيَةُ * وَحَبْلٌ إِنْ ضَمَمْتَ عَلَى التَّمَادِي
وَبِفَتْحِ العَيْنِ (عَمْرٌ) وَبِالكَسْرِ (عِمْرٌ) وَبِالضَّمِّ (عُمْرٌ) لِلعُمْرِ الطَّوِيلِ وَعُمْرَانِ المَنَازِلِ اهـ

english_lines: With Fatḥah (Laḥā) it denotes disputation; with Kasrah (Liḥā), plural of beard-jaw; with Ḍammah (Luḥā), the hair of the chin.
With Fatḥah (Malā) it is an open desert plain; with Kasrah (Milā), the fullness of a vessel; with Ḍammah (Mulā), fine wraps and garments.
With Fatḥah (Shakl) it means likeness and counterpart; with Kasrah (Shikl), graceful coquetry; with Ḍammah (Shukl), plural of hobble/fetter.
With Fatḥah (Ṣarrah) it denotes a throng/company; with Kasrah (Ṣirrah), intense frost; with Ḍammah (Ṣurrah), a purse of gold or silver coin.
With Fatḥah (Rammah) it means repairing what is decayed; with Kasrah (Rimmah), decayed bones; with Ḍammah (Rummah), a worn piece of rope.
And with Fatḥah/Ḍammah (ʿAmr / ʿUmr) it denotes long life-span and the flourishing cultivation of abodes. [End]
hashiyah_lines: حاشية: تقول صررتُ مالي في الصُّرَّة صرّاً، وأخذته برُمَّته أي بجميعه، صح.
